name: Deeprun Tram
summary: The Deeprun Tram carries travelers beneath the earth between Ironforge and Stormwind City. King Magni Bronzebeard commissioned it after the Second War, and its twin tracks now carry citizens, soldiers, and goods between the Alliance capitals.

sections.title: A Marvel of Subterranean Engineering
sections.body: King Magni Bronzebeard wanted dwarven aid and supplies to reach Stormwind faster after the Second War. Mountain passes slowed the journey, so he asked High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque to design an underground railway. Gnomish engineers cut the route beneath a mountain and through a vast subterranean lake. Rats plagued the excavation, but the tram was completed. It carries thousands of travelers between Ironforge and Stormwind without charge.

faq.q: Why was the Deeprun Tram built?
faq.answer: After the Second War, King Magni Bronzebeard needed a faster route for supplies and dwarven troops helping to rebuild and defend Stormwind. He commissioned High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque to design and build the underground railway linking the two capitals.

faq.q: How does the tram travel underwater?
faq.answer: Gnomish engineers breached a vast subterranean lake while digging between Dun Morogh and Stormwind. They built a sealed, reinforced glass tunnel through the water, where passengers can watch threshadons and sharks swim beside the track.

faq.q: Why are there so many rats along the tracks?
faq.answer: The dark, damp shafts along the tracks give vermin a place to breed. Gnomish station masters struggle to keep rats from chewing cables and overrunning platforms, and sometimes travelers and rat catchers like Monty help thin their numbers.

faq.q: Is the tram free to ride?
faq.answer: Yes. Ironforge and Stormwind sponsor the tram as a civic and military service. It runs continuously without fare for citizens and Alliance allies.

angles.text: The railway is a gnomish engineering achievement, with advanced track propulsion, reinforced glasswork built to withstand the depths of a subterranean lake, and intricate electrical switching stations.
For the Alliance, the tram connects two of its most fortified capitals. It allows troops to move quickly between them and supports their mutual defense.
